A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Textured Gaussians research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, quantitative comparisons, custom-scene reconstructions, and texture/Gaussian ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds the authors' DTU baseline runs, efficiency measurements, and geometry and rendering-artifact diagnostics.

M1.justification: The texture representation, ray-Gaussian intersection, rendering equations, loss, and two-stage optimization remain unchanged. V2's statement about dynamically selecting the intersection plane elaborates the two-major-axis construction already described in v1; no changed procedure is established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Blender, Mip-NeRF 360, DTU, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending scenes, plus the same two custom art-gallery captures. Added comparisons and diagnostics use retained coverage. Dynamic-scene reconstruction is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Mip-NeRF 360 and Instant-NGP to the DTU comparison and Xu et al.'s Texture-GS to the Blender comparison. The Blender Texture-GS results are attributed to the GStex authors' runs. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New DTU baseline experiments introduce documented configurations, including Mip-NeRF 360's black-background settings and near/far clipping planes of 2 and 6. V2 also adds resource evaluation aggregated over 26 scenes with equal Gaussian counts and 4x4 RGBA textures. Existing training and dataset protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds computational efficiency analysis in Table A.2, effective-rank distributions examining Gaussian shape in Figure A.2, and grazing-view ablations of intersection clipping and SH base colors in Figure A.3. The existing texture-type, resolution, Gaussian-count, and color-decomposition analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added. The new effective-rank histograms describe Gaussian geometry; experimental uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds DTU results of 34.28/0.9641/0.0698 for Mip-NeRF 360 and 23.58/0.7653/0.2603 for Instant-NGP, plus Blender Texture-GS results of 28.97/0.9380/0.0550, in PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS order. Mip-NeRF 360 now leads DTU PSNR over the unchanged 33.61 for Ours. Table A.2 and Figures A.2-A.3 add resource, shape, and artifact findings; previously reported results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10) and (A.1)-(A.6), including the rendering and densification formulations, are unchanged. The added effective-rank discussion supplies empirical interpretation and a citation, without introducing a mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: per-Gaussian textures increase expressivity, alpha-only textures offer a useful quality/storage tradeoff, and reconstruction improves at comparable Gaussian counts or model sizes. The rewritten abstract preserves their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: V2 uses the rank distributions to justify approximating 2D Gaussians within the 3DGS framework and adds evidence-based explanations of grazing-view artifact controls. It explicitly acknowledges memory and rendering overhead in the efficiency analysis and proposes time-varying textures for future dynamic-scene reconstruction.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds baseline-code links, configuration filenames, background flags, and clipping bounds for the new DTU experiments. It also explicitly describes dynamic intersection-plane selection. Appendix D supplies concrete model-size, GPU-memory, and inference-time measurements; the existing implementation and optimization details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references, including HDGS, BBSplat, SuperGaussians, and effective-rank analysis. The concurrent-work paragraph expands beyond GStex and emphasizes alpha textures and analysis of texture variants as distinguishing contributions. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and several captions and paragraphs are condensed or polished. V2 expands selected related-work, experimental-detail, and discussion passages and adds an acknowledgment. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds efficiency Table A.2 and diagnostic Figures A.2-A.3. The previous Figure A.2 becomes Figure A.4 on a separate page, with subsequent appendix displays renumbered. Existing figure content is retained, alongside localized caption edits and text reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 fills missing baseline comparisons, documents the DTU runs, and strengthens support for existing design choices through measured resource costs and targeted diagnostics. These improve completeness and transparency. A material inconsistency remains: Appendix C retains v1's claim of approximately equal inference time, whereas new Table A.2 reports 0.123 seconds per frame for Textured Gaussians versus 0.073 for 3DGS.
